summary: The client-contract check completed, closing the third consequence of the multi-voter finding. Receipt 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db resolves both comparisons: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, the node isolated with one committed voter won leadership and its client Apply returned success (comparison 0 violated, witness event index 27, minority_leader and minority_apply_ok true), while the flag-off control produced no leader on that side and no acknowledgement (comparison 1 holds, evaluated event index 29, with the majority side acknowledging its own write). Together with the two earlier complete comparisons — configuration loss (witness index 15, control 18) and minority election (witness index 22 with the majority side still holding a leader, control 25) — the child question is answered as violated with defect_claim asserted: after a restart with this flag the node keeps the snapshot's smaller configuration, its quorum arithmetic follows that stale list, and both the leadership decision and a client acknowledgement can rest on a minority of the committed configuration. A Behavior knowledge entry is promoted for the acknowledged write with that receipt, the interpretation carries joint history across the three complete executions of the same scenario, and the limits are explicit: no FSM divergence or lost acknowledged entry is witnessed because no run had a majority-side leader writing concurrently, windows are bounded so no frequency or absence is claimed, and the registered gap stays open only on that divergence point.
